ety.text: From Middle English neighebour, neighbour, neyghebour, from Old English nēahġebūr (“neighbour”), from Proto-West Germanic *nāhwagabūrō, from Proto-Germanic *nēhwagabūrô (“neighbour”, literally “near-dweller”), from *nēhwaz (“close, near”) + *gabūrô (“dweller”). Equivalent to nigh (“near”) + bower (“farmer”).

senses.d: A person living on adjacent or nearby land; a person situated adjacently or nearby; anything (of the same type of thing as the subject) in an adjacent or nearby position.
ex: My neighbour has two noisy cats.
They′re our neighbours across the street.

senses.d: One who is near in sympathy or confidence.
ex: Buckingham / No more shall be the neighbour to my counsel.

senses.d: A fellow human being.
Anything located directly adjacent to something else.
ex: The flood fill algorithm fills an area with colour by starting at one pixel and recursively visiting its neighbours.

senses.d: To be adjacent to
ex: Though France neighbours Germany, its culture is significantly different.
Theſe grow at the South end of the Iland, and on the leiſurely aſcending hills that neighbour the ſhore.

senses.d: To be similar to, to be almost the same as.
ex: That sort of talk is neighbouring on treason.

senses.d: To associate intimately with; to be close to.
ex: […] the barbarous Scythyan, […] / Shall bee as well neighbour’d, pittyed and relieued / As thou my ſometime daughter.

ety.text: From an alteration of earlier neighborred (“neighborhood”), from Middle English neȝeburredde, neheborreden, equivalent to neighbor + -red; the term being interpreted as neighbor + -hood. For change in suffix (-red to -hood), compare brotherhood. Cognates Cognate with Scots nichbourheid (“neighbourhood”). Compare also Dutch naburigheid (“neighbourhood”).

senses.d: The residential area near one's home.
ex: He lives in my neighborhood.

senses.d: The inhabitants of a residential area.
ex: The fire alarmed the neighborhood.

senses.d: A formal or informal division of a municipality or region.
ex: We have just moved to a pleasant neighborhood.

senses.d: An approximate amount.
ex: He must be making in the neighborhood of $200,000 per year.

senses.d: The quality of physical proximity.
ex: The slums and the palace were in awful neighborhood.

senses.d: The quality of being a neighbor, of living nearby, next to each other; proximity.
ex: Our neighborhood was our only reason to exchange hollow greetings.
Then the prison and the palace were in awful neighbourhood.
